claimed_purpose.text: Persistent memory for AI agents and coding tools, covering semantic facts, episodic events, and procedural workflows with a success/failure track record.
Hybrid retrieval engine combining vector search and graph traversal to assemble structured context for an AI agent
Local vector store sufficient for vaults up to ~10K notes, intended to be replaceable at larger scale
Mengram stores memories and profile data for users across hosted and self-hosted deployments.

mechanisms.text: Retrieve path is hybrid: semantic vector search (top-K by score, min_score=0.25) followed by graph expansion (multi-hop neighbors), with fallback to graph text search then raw text search then procedure search
Facts carry optional temporal metadata; temporal resolution is mandatory when date context is available — relative terms like 'yesterday' must be resolved to absolute dates
Procedure versions track violated_assumption, preconditions, success_count, and fail_count, so agents loading a version know what to verify before trusting the workflow.
Isolation: vault_path is a constructor parameter, implying per-user or per-agent isolation is achieved by instantiating MengramBrain with a different vault directory
Three distinct memory types are persisted: semantic (facts/preferences), episodic (events/decisions/outcomes), and procedural (workflows that evolve from failures)
Setup writes credentials to shell rc files (bashrc/zshrc) and sets them in-process, but on Windows this path is dead; only config.json actually persists.
Mengram's MCP server loads a profile on initialization; a failure in this step is surfaced in the instructions field of the initialize response.
Mengram exposes a 'recall' tool via its MCP server, accepting a query and user_id as arguments, indicating retrieval of memories keyed by user.
Proposed fix adds a credential resolver for base_url mirroring the existing key resolver, with env-var → config.json → default fallback chain.
Extraction produces five distinct memory types: entities (with typed facts), relations, knowledge artifacts, episodes, and procedures
Existing memory context is injected into the extraction prompt to enable deduplication and consistent entity naming across sessions
The OpenClaw integration installs Mengram as a skill (static documentation/scripts) rather than a plugin with lifecycle hooks.
save-conversation.sh POSTs conversation text to /v1/add_text with a JSON payload containing the text and source field.
Episodes carry an importance score (0.0–1.0) and emotional valence, enabling future ranked or filtered retrieval
Current VectorStore API surface includes add, search (with top_k and min_score), stats(), and search_by_entity()
Mengram provides a /v1/memories REST endpoint, suggesting a persistent store of memories accessible via API.
All hook exit paths are silent by design, providing no visibility into whether a hook fired or what it did.
Knowledge graph is lazily rebuilt from vault on first access after any remember() call invalidates it
MCP tools named recall and remember are the named interfaces for retrieval and write operations.
Mengram has a current decay model for episodic memory based on half-life of individual events
add() writes new facts and events from a conversation into memory, scoped per user_id
Cloud retrieval uses Cohere multilingual embeddings and rerank across 23 languages
One API call to profile() scaffolds the LLM system prompt with full user context
Data cannot be deleted according to the developer's own data safety declaration
Mengram maintains indexes, embeddings, and caches associated with an account.
Cloud uses pgvector with 1536-dim vectors, separate from local engine

ledger.claim: Pre-compaction hook writes working state before compaction and restores it verbatim after; session-start hook re-injects cognitive profile after every /clear or compaction.
ledger.quote:
Session Start → Loads your cognitive profile (fires after /clear, compaction, and restarts)
Every Prompt → Searches past sessions for relevant context (auto-recall)
After Response → Saves new knowledge in background (auto-save)

ledger.claim: Host/tool isolation excludes facts recorded under a different OS or tool from being injected into the current session; excluded fact count is reported as facts_left_out_for_host.
ledger.quote: so a workspace path recorded on your Mac never reaches a Claude Code session on a Linux box, and a Cursor settings fact never reaches Codex — those are left out and counted (`facts_left_out_for_host`)

ledger.claim: Local mode uses a memfmt Markdown folder as the store with atomic per-file writes, a folder lock for concurrent sessions, and no embeddings for search.
